newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Exiled Cambodia prince puts off return - royalists.
newsitem.headline: Exiled Cambodia prince puts off return - royalists.

text.p: Cambodia's exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh, accused of plotting to kill Co-Premier Hun Sen, has put off plans to return home next week, a top royalist military officer said on Friday.
"Sirivudh will not return as the situation is bad and there is no amnesty from the king," Lieutenant General Nhiek Bun Chhay told reporters.
Sirivudh is King Norodom Sihanouk's half brother.
Another member of the royalist FUNCINPEC party, Interior Ministry Secretary of State Hor Sok, also said the prince would not return. He gave no more details.

Sirivudh was exiled in December 1995 after being held for a month for allegedly plotting to assassinate Hun Sen. He had said he planned to return on April 14 for the Cambodian new year with or without a royal amnesty.
Hun Sen on Thursday warned violence could erupt between his Cambodian People's Party and FUNCINPEC if the prince returned.

The two parties formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run general elections in 1993 and tensions have been high since a deadly grenade attack on a March 30 demonstration held by opposition leader and FUNCINPEC ally Sam Rainsy.
Both the king and First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh this week urged Sirivudh not to return.
Sihanouk wrote to Ranariddh saying he would not make an enemy of Hun Sen by granting an amnesty to Sirivudh. He warned that he would resign immediately if the affair were settled by violence.
